properties.name: Jezero Crater (Perseverance)
pros: Ancient river delta rich in hydrated minerals
Low elevation (-2.5 km) gives denser atmosphere for braking
Near-equatorial latitude (18.4°N) provides warm solar conditions
risks: Steep delta scarps and boulder fields nearby
No shallow pure water-ice sheet directly at the surface
resources: Fine basaltic regolith for 3D-printed radiation shielding

properties.name: Gale Crater (Curiosity)
pros: Very deep basin (-4.5 km) provides thick atmospheric column and lower radiation
Equatorial location (-4.6°S) maximizes solar power and moderates temperatures
Smooth Bradbury Landing plains for safe touchdowns
risks: Steep slopes ascending Aeolis Mons (Mount Sharp)
Sharp wind-eroded ventifacts that can damage rover wheels
resources: Sulfate and clay mineral beds holding bound water
Natural topographic wind shelter inside crater floor

properties.name: Elysium Planitia (InSight)
pros: Known as the 'biggest parking lot on Mars' — exceptionally flat and smooth
Equatorial latitude (4.5°N) ideal for solar arrays
Low elevation (-2.6 km) supports heavy lander deceleration
risks: Frequent dust accumulation on solar panels
Low subsurface water ice availability at equatorial latitude
resources: Deep unconsolidated regolith (~3–5 m) easy to excavate for berms
Flat terrain for large habitat & solar farm deployment

properties.name: Vastitas Borealis (Phoenix)
pros: Confirmed shallow water-ice table just centimeters beneath the soil
Very low northern plains elevation (-4.1 km) with dense atmosphere
risks: Extreme polar winter darkness and CO2 frost burial (68.2°N)
Severe cold (-100°C+) requires nuclear/kilopower instead of solar
resources: Abundant near-surface water ice for life support & methalox propellant
Dense atmospheric CO2 for Sabatier fuel synthesis
